statement: Whenever max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, r is the maximum cardinality of a set M of pairs (i, j) such that: (a) 0 <= i < len(nums1) and 0 <= j < len(nums2); (b) nums1[i] = nums2[j]; (c) no two distinct pairs in M have the same first coordinate and no two distinct pairs in M have the same second coordinate; and (d) for any two distinct pairs (i, j) and (i', j') in M, if i < i' then j < j'. The empty set is allowed. Equivalently, r is the length of a longest common subsequence of nums1 and nums2.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are integers with 1 <= len(nums1) <= 500 and 1 <= len(nums2) <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 1 <= nums1[i] <= 2000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 1 <= nums2[j] <= 2000.

statement: The call max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns a result r and does not fail: it does not panic, go out of bounds, or overflow. The returned i64 represents a nonnegative mathematical integer.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are integers with 1 <= len(nums1) <= 500 and 1 <= len(nums2) <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 1 <= nums1[i] <= 2000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 1 <= nums2[j] <= 2000.

statement: Whenever max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, 0 <= r <= min(len(nums1), len(nums2)).
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are integers with 1 <= len(nums1) <= 500 and 1 <= len(nums2) <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 1 <= nums1[i] <= 2000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 1 <= nums2[j] <= 2000.

statement: Whenever max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, there exists a set M of exactly r pairs (i, j) such that: (a) 0 <= i < len(nums1) and 0 <= j < len(nums2); (b) nums1[i] = nums2[j]; (c) no two distinct pairs in M have the same first coordinate and no two distinct pairs in M have the same second coordinate; and (d) for any two distinct pairs (i, j) and (i', j') in M, if i < i' then j < j'.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are integers with 1 <= len(nums1) <= 500 and 1 <= len(nums2) <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 1 <= nums1[i] <= 2000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 1 <= nums2[j] <= 2000.

statement: Whenever max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, every set M of pairs (i, j) satisfying (a) 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= j < len(nums2), (b) nums1[i] = nums2[j], (c) no two distinct pairs in M have the same first coordinate and no two distinct pairs in M have the same second coordinate, and (d) for any two distinct pairs (i, j) and (i', j') in M, if i < i' then j < j', has cardinality at most r.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are integers with 1 <= len(nums1) <= 500 and 1 <= len(nums2) <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 1 <= nums1[i] <= 2000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 1 <= nums2[j] <= 2000.

statement: For every nums1 and nums2 satisfying the preconditions, if max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns r and max_uncrossed_lines(nums2, nums1) returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are integers with 1 <= len(nums1) <= 500 and 1 <= len(nums2) <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 1 <= nums1[i] <= 2000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 1 <= nums2[j] <= 2000.

statement: Let rev1 be the array of length len(nums1) defined by rev1[i] = nums1[len(nums1) - 1 - i] for 0 <= i < len(nums1), and let rev2 be the array of length len(nums2) defined by rev2[j] = nums2[len(nums2) - 1 - j] for 0 <= j < len(nums2). If max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns r and max_uncrossed_lines(rev1, rev2) returns r', then r = r'.

statement: Whenever max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, r = 1 if there exists an index j with 0 <= j < len(nums2) and nums2[j] = nums1[0], and r = 0 otherwise.

statement: Whenever max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if there is no pair (i, j) with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= j < len(nums2), and nums1[i] = nums2[j].

statement: Whenever max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, r = min(len(nums1), len(nums2)).
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are integers with 1 <= len(nums1) <= 500 and 1 <= len(nums2) <= 500; there exists an integer c with 1 <= c <= 2000 such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), nums1[i] = c, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), nums2[j] = c.

statement: Whenever max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, r <= sum_{c=1}^{2000} min(count1(c), count2(c)), where count1(c) is the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums1) and nums1[i] = c, and count2(c) is the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(nums2) and nums2[j] = c.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are integers with 1 <= len(nums1) <= 500 and 1 <= len(nums2) <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 1 <= nums1[i] <= 2000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 1 <= nums2[j] <= 2000.

statement: Let p1 be the slice consisting of nums1[0], nums1[1], ..., nums1[len(nums1) - 2], and let p2 be the slice consisting of nums2[0], nums2[1], ..., nums2[len(nums2) - 2]. If max_uncrossed_lines(p1, p2) returns s and max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns r, then r = s + 1.

statement: Let nums1' be nums1 followed by extra1, and let nums2' be nums2 followed by extra2. If max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns r and max_uncrossed_lines(nums1', nums2') returns r', then r' >= r.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are integers with 1 <= len(nums1) <= 500 and 1 <= len(nums2) <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 1 <= nums1[i] <= 2000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 1 <= nums2[j] <= 2000; extra1 and extra2 are finite arrays of integers in the range 1 <= value <= 2000 such that len(nums1) + len(extra1) <= 500 and len(nums2) + len(extra2) <= 500.

statement: Let p1 be the slice consisting of nums1[0], ..., nums1[len(nums1)-2] and let p2 be the slice consisting of nums2[0], ..., nums2[len(nums2)-2]. If max_uncrossed_lines(p1, nums2) returns s1, max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, p2) returns s2, and max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns r, then r = max(s1, s2).
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are integers with 2 <= len(nums1) <= 500 and 2 <= len(nums2) <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 1 <= nums1[i] <= 2000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 1 <= nums2[j] <= 2000; nums1[len(nums1)-1] != nums2[len(nums2)-1].

statement: Whenever max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, r equals the number of integers c with 1 <= c <= 2000 such that c occurs in nums1 and c occurs in nums2.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are integers with 1 <= len(nums1) <= 500 and 1 <= len(nums2) <= 500; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 1 <= nums1[i] <= 2000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 1 <= nums2[j] <= 2000; nums1 is strictly increasing (nums1[i] < nums1[i+1] for 0 <= i < len(nums1)-1) and nums2 is strictly increasing (nums2[j] < nums2[j+1] for 0 <= j < len(nums2)-1).

statement: Whenever max_uncrossed_lines(nums1, nums2) returns a result r, r = 1 if there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(nums1) and nums1[i] = nums2[0], and r = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums1) <= 500, len(nums2) = 1; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 1 <= nums1[i] <= 2000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 1 <= nums2[j] <= 2000.
